title: Aggregate zig build test-integration is unstable in workspace r-co-2: unrelated failures and multi-minute hangs block clean verification signal
summary: While attempting to re-verify ISS-0054/GH-283 (ADP-09/ADP-10 assertion behavior) via a real test run, two independent `zig build test-integration` runs against workspace r-co-2's test DB (port 5453) each surfaced different unrelated pre-existing failures (sch303_timer_dlq_test, env01_test, env02_test, iss0185_dual_schema_test, iss0605_orphan_self_heal_test) without ever completing cleanly. Neither run reached a usable ADP-09/ADP-10 result. The second run stalled with zero log growth for 10+ minutes on the same binary (env01/env02) and had to be killed. There is no scoped `zig build test-integration-adp09` / `-adp10` step to isolate a specific requirement's tests from the unstable aggregate suite, which is what made isolating a clean signal for GH-283 impossible in this pass.

root_cause.details:
Root-caused via a clean-DB-reset control run (fresh db_test container + volume, fresh `zig build migrate`, single `zig build test-integration` invocation, no accumulated long-lived-workspace state). Two independent, precisely-identified mechanisms were found, neither of which is 'accumulated workspace state' or 'genuine per-test flakiness':

1. (Fixed in this run) `tests/integration/iss105_token_model_test.zig`'s TC-ISS-105-03 queried `pg_indexes WHERE tablename='instance_projections' AND indexname='idx_instance_active_tokens'` with no `schemaname` filter. `pg_indexes` is not search_path-scoped -- it returns one row per schema containing a same-named index. Because `instance_projections`/its GIN index are provisioned into multiple schemas (public, tenant_default, and any tenant schema a concurrently-running sibling binary provisions during a parallel run), the query legitimately returned 3 rows instead of 1 whenever concurrent tenant-schema provisioning happened to be in flight. This was a genuine, deterministic query bug (missing schema scoping), not a race in the sense of nondeterministic timing -- it was just made *visible* by concurrency. Fixed directly by adding a `pg_table_is_visible((schemaname || '.' || indexname)::regclass)` filter, matching the search_path-aware pattern the file's own `pg_attribute`/`::regclass` query one block above already used.

2. (Root-caused, NOT fixed in this run -- forwarded as ISS-0659/GH-681) PR #494 (closing GH-486/ISS-0162, merged prior to this run) fixed a class of cross-binary data race by having `TestHarness.init()` hold an advisory lock for its full lifetime, serializing `TestHarness`-based binaries against each other so `resetTestData()`'s unconditional DELETEs on shared tables (timers, events, dead_letter_items, instance_projections, tasks, process_definitions, ...) cannot wipe a concurrently-running `TestHarness`-based sibling's fixtures. That fix's scope is TestHarness-to-TestHarness only. A grep of tests/integration/*.zig found 31 files (including sch303_timer_dlq_test.zig, env01_test.zig, env02_test.zig, env05_test.zig, spt01 reads shared public.tenant rows these mutate, and 27 others) that manage their own db.Pool directly and never acquire that lock. These remain exposed to being wiped by, or interfering with, any TestHarness sibling running concurrently under the ~30-binary `test-integration-others-internal` barrier (which Zig's build runner parallelizes up to `-j` = all CPU cores, 16 on this host, with no other mutual exclusion between siblings beyond the one-time `clean_test_db` predecessor for the whole group). This directly explains sch303 (timers row deleted mid-poll), env01/spt01 (public.tenant/tenant_schemas row-count races), iss0185 (tenant_default HYBRID-table duplicate-count races), and is a plausible contributor to env05's provisionTenantSchema failure under heavy concurrent migration-replay load. The originally-reported 'hangs' were re-examined directly against live pg_stat_activity during this run's control pass: no true deadlock or blocked-forever wait was found -- what looks like a 10+ minute silent stall is explained by (a) tenant-schema provisioning replaying the full 124-file migration set per schema, serially, per test, which is genuinely slow under 16-way concurrent DB load, and (b) the aggregate suite producing zero stdout during normal (non-failing) test execution, so a slow-but-live run is visually indistinguishable from a hang until either it finishes or Zig's own 'test runner failed to respond' watchdog fires (observed multiple times in this control run -- a real diagnostic signal, not a false one).

evidence.discovered_during: Batch re-triage of GH-280..301 (WF03-batch-GH280-301-triage-20260810), attempting to verify GH-283/ISS-0054
evidence.symptom_1: Run 1: zig build test-integration surfaced failures in sch303_timer_dlq_test, env01_test, env02_test, iss0185_dual_schema_test, iss0605_orphan_self_heal_test — none of these are related to ADP-09/ADP-10 or to any change made in this triage pass (read-only pass, no source edits)
evidence.symptom_2: Run 2: same command stalled with zero log growth for 10+ minutes on env01_test/env02_test, had to be killed; did not reach ADP-09/ADP-10
evidence.control_run_2026_08_10: docker-compose down -v db_test && up -d db_test (fresh volume) -> BPM_DB_URL=$BPM_TEST_DB_URL zig build migrate (124 migrations, exit 0) -> single zig build test-integration invocation (~12 min wall clock, did NOT hang, completed with exit 1). Result: 94/111 build steps succeeded, 14 failed; 1010/1027 tests passed, 7 failed. 9 distinct files failed: sch303_timer_dlq_test, spt01_iss0068_onboarding_schema_test, iss105_token_model_test (fixed in this run), iss0185_dual_schema_test, env01_test, env05_test (all 5 remaining -- Race-B-class, forwarded to ISS-0659/GH-681), plus api03_instance_read_test/adp06_pipeline_run_correlation_test/sim01_04_simulation_mode_test (allocator leaks -- different symptom class, not investigated, not claimed as resolved or forwarded by this issue). This is broader than the originally-observed 5 files, confirming the instability is systemic (concurrency-driven) rather than tied to those 5 specific files or to accumulated workspace state -- a truly clean DB still reproduces a similar-sized failure set.
evidence.live_lock_check: During the control run, pg_stat_activity and pg_locks were queried directly while the suite was mid-flight and appeared to stall by log-growth alone. No blocked-waiting-on-lock chain was found (a pg_locks self-join for ungranted locks returned 0 rows at every sample); instead, active connections were found genuinely executing migration-replay SQL (provisionTenantSchema running individual migration files sequentially per tenant schema) -- i.e. slow and quiet, not deadlocked.

affected_areas: tests/integration/ (31-file TestHarness-lock-scope gap -- forwarded to ISS-0659/GH-681)
build.zig (test-integration step; added test-integration-adp09/-adp10 scoped steps in this run)

recommended_fix_strategy.primary_action: ISSUE-FIXER to reproduce with a clean db_test reset (docker-compose down -v db_test && up -d db_test, fresh zig build migrate) as a control, to separate genuine flakiness from accumulated long-lived-workspace state.
recommended_fix_strategy.secondary_action: Add scoped zig build test-integration-<slug> steps for high-value targets (at minimum adp09/adp10, since GH-283 needs isolation from the aggregate suite to get a clean signal) — generally useful beyond this issue.
recommended_fix_strategy.what_NOT_to_do: Do not treat this as proof that env01/env02/sch303/iss0185/iss0605 are broken — they were incidental noise during an unrelated verification attempt, not diagnosed themselves. Do not fold their diagnosis into this issue without separately confirming each is a real regression rather than environment noise.
recommended_fix_strategy.status_note: Both the primary and secondary recommended actions were completed in this run (WF03-GH679-20260810). The clean-reset control run was performed and is the basis of the root_cause above. adp09/adp10 scoped build steps were added. Per the original what_NOT_to_do guidance, individual diagnosis of sch303/env01/iss0185/env05 (env02 was NOT among the 9 failures in the clean control run, and iss0605 also did not reproduce) was NOT folded into this issue beyond identifying their shared root-cause mechanism -- that mechanism is forwarded as its own issue (ISS-0659/GH-681) per CLAUDE.md's Unblock-Everything scope boundary, since fully fixing it requires touching up to 31 test files plus helpers.zig and is a separate, larger undertaking than this issue's own recommended-fix scope contemplated.

resolution: 1) Fixed tests/integration/iss105_token_model_test.zig's TC-ISS-105-03 pg_indexes query to filter by pg_table_is_visible(), eliminating the schema-scoping bug that made it fail under concurrent tenant-schema provisioning. 2) Added test-integration-adp09 and test-integration-adp10 scoped build steps to build.zig (these two ADP files existed on disk but were previously wired into NO build step at all -- not the aggregate, not scoped -- so GH-283/ISS-0054 could never get any signal from them, isolated or otherwise, until now). 3) Root-caused the remaining instability (sch303_timer_dlq_test, spt01_iss0068_onboarding_schema_test, iss0185_dual_schema_test, env01_test, env05_test) to a precise, evidenced mechanism -- 31 integration test files bypass TestHarness's PR #494 advisory-lock protection -- and forwarded it as ISS-0659/GH-681 (MAJOR, queued) rather than attempting a full fix in this run, per the original issue's own what_NOT_to_do guidance and CLAUDE.md's Unblock-Everything scope boundary (this is a multi-file systemic fix, not a direct blocker of THIS issue's stated deliverables). 4) Determined that the originally-reported 'hangs' are not true deadlocks -- live lock-graph inspection during a live slow stretch found genuine (if slow) migration-replay activity, not a blocked-forever wait; documented this so future diagnosis does not re-chase a hang theory that live evidence does not support. 3 allocator-leak failures (api03_instance_read_test, adp06_pipeline_run_correlation_test, sim01_04_simulation_mode_test) were observed in the same control run but are explicitly NOT investigated or claimed as resolved by this issue -- a structurally different symptom (memory leak vs. data race/assertion mismatch).
verification: zig build: exit 0, no 'error set' output. zig build test: exit 0 (all unit tests pass). zig build migrate: exit 0, idempotent (124 applied then 0 pending on re-run). zig build test-integration-iss105: all 4 tests pass (verified after the fix, with BPM_TEST_DB_URL correctly pointed at this workspace's port 5453 -- caught and worked around a stale-bashrc BPM_TEST_DB_URL=...5434 reassertion between shell invocations, consistent with this workspace's already-documented rco-bashrc-stale-test-db-url gotcha). zig build test-integration-adp09: all 5 tests pass. zig build test-integration-adp10: all tests pass. python3 tools/lint_sql_param_types.py src tests: 0 BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR. python3 tools/lint_test_isolation.py tests/integration: OK, no isolation issues. Did not re-run the full aggregate zig build test-integration a third time in this session: a single clean run already takes ~12 minutes and the remaining 5 failures are explicitly forwarded (not claimed fixed), so a second full-aggregate run would not change this issue's disposition -- the scoped-step verifications above directly confirm the two changes this issue's resolution claims (iss105 fix, adp09/adp10 wiring).
prevention: Long-lived integration test workspaces should be periodically reset (fresh db_test volume) to rule out accumulated state as a source of flakiness before diagnosing individual test failures. NOTE: this run's control test found this was NOT the dominant factor here -- a truly fresh workspace reproduced a similar-sized failure set, so this remains good practice but is not sufficient on its own; see ISS-0659 for the concurrency mechanism that a reset does not fix.

Scoped test-integration-<slug> build steps for specific requirement clusters make it possible to get a clean signal on one requirement without depending on the full aggregate suite's stability — relevant to GH-297 (PI-07 gate tiering) as well. adp09/adp10 now have these steps.

New integration test files that touch shared tables (timers, events, dead_letter_items, instance_projections, tasks, process_definitions, public.tenant, public.tenant_schemas, or tenant_default's DDL objects) should use TestHarness, not a raw db.Pool, specifically to inherit PR #494's advisory-lock protection -- see ISS-0659/GH-681.

Unscoped pg_catalog view queries (pg_indexes, pg_tables, pg_class without a schemaname/regclass qualifier) are a latent bug class in a codebase where the same table name is deliberately provisioned into multiple schemas (public/tenant_default/per-tenant) -- worth a dedicated lint pass across the other 12 files identified with similar unqualified pg_catalog queries during this investigation (not enumerated individually here; grep 'FROM pg_indexes\|FROM pg_tables' tests/integration/*.zig for candidates).
